title: REAL A(*) — assumed-size array loses N; out-of-bounds is undefined
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE SUM_ARR(A, N, S)
C     A(*) tells the compiler 'A is a 1-D array whose upper bound is
C     not known here'. The caller-supplied N is the actual length.
C     The callee MUST honour N -- accessing A(N+1) is undefined.
C     Translating to Java's float[] gives a length field for free,
C     but legacy callers may pass N off-by-one and rely on the
C     unchecked F77 behaviour.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER N, I
      REAL    A(*), S
      S = 0.0
      DO I = 1, N
         S = S + A(I)
      END DO
      END
notes: Assumed-size arrays (A(*)) are everywhere in legacy F77 numerical libraries. The N argument is the actual contract — a Java rewrite to float[] gets a length 'for free' but legacy callers may pass N != A.length deliberately (e.g. processing a sub-vector). The spec must surface N as the authoritative length AND ask the SME whether 0 < N <= ACTUAL_LENGTH is invariant or assumption.
